findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the upright white cooler closest to the door if the kitchen to measure 50F with the infrared probe. This cooler failure must be a recent occurrence, as the yogurt within the cooler measured 41F with a probe thermometer. All TCS foods within the cooler was transferred to an alternative cold holding unit. PIC was made aware of the failure and plans to contact maintenance. Since the facility has adequate cold holding equipment aside from the cooler that failed, this violation is considered corrected on site with no follow-up needed. Inspector will call occasionally to spot check cooler repair process.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector observed no food handler’s certificates available at the facility. The PIC was informed and has an action plan to certify all kitchen staff. The PIC currently operating the kitchen as a CFPM from previous employment. Ensure all kitchen staff have food handler’s or food manager’s by next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employee put on new gloves without first washing hands. Discussed proper glove use with employee. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed copies of employee health reporting agreements were not available for the GM or any of the staff that work in the breakfast area. Employee health documents were provided and discussed. GM and staff present at the time of inspection signed reporting agreements. Ensure all staff that will work and/or have the potential to help in the breakfast area are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
 The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)
Observed 3 part sink made to have less than than 100ppm of quat sanitizer. The water was 60F. The automatic dispenser mixes sanitizer with cold water below 75F.  The water is so cold that the employees do not like to use it so they add hot water from the sink which decreases the concentration of the the solution. The employees are going to discontinue use of the automatic dispenser and mix sanitizer by hand so that it is at minimum 75F and tests with a test strip to be at least 200ppm. Always follow label directions.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-901.11: After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) shall be air dried or used after adequate draining before FOOD contact. (B) May not be cloth dried except that UTENSISL that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are clean and dry. 
Observed the kitchen employee to be drying pans with a cloth towel. The employee was coached and will allow items to air dry form now on.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 
Observed the in use box a single use gloves to be stored under the hand soap dispenser at the hand sink. The gloves were removed. Do not store single use gloves where they can become contaminated with splash or soap.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: 4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. Gaskets on the upright refrigerator and Upright freezer doors are in disrepair. Replace the damaged gaskets.
findings.citation_text: 4-202.11 Food-Contact surface at dish drying area is no longer smooth and easily clean able as towels from the hotel have been placed on them. A food-contact surface that is not smooth and easily clean able can harbor bacteria that can be transfered to food. Replace with a National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI approved surface.  Provide drain racks for proper, clean drying area. Towels were removed. Wash dishes and properly drain dry before use.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  
Provide verifiable proof of handler certified employees. Employees who are not certified managers must have certified hander training within 30 days of hire.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Breakfast attendant was observed going between tasks and multiple glove changes without washing hands. In one instance, the attendant was washing dishes and did not wash hands between glove changes before continuing on to food preparation. Handwashing between tasks and glove changes were discussed.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, and prior to putting on gloves.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the handwashing sink in the kitchen. Handwashing signs were provided and posted during inspection.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 In-use tub of whipped butter was observed out on the counter in the kitchen. Internal temperature was observed at 68F-70F. Directions for storage on the lid state to keep refrigerated at 34F-40F. Remaining portion was to be used or discarded by the end of breakfast service. Attendant was advised the whole tub of whipped butter should remain in the cooler and only a small portion removed for use. Any remaining portion must be discarded at the end of breakfast once removed from the original container and held at room temperature during breakfast service. Another tub of whipped butter was also observed out in the storage area. It was still at 39F and was out for ~15 minutes. Whipped butter was placed back in the cooler.    

Cream cheese packets in the bottom of the glass front counter top cooler in the breakfast area had internal temperatures of 46F-47F. Yogurts on the other shelving in the cooler were observed at internal temperatures of 39F-43F depending on location within the cooler. Plastic storage bins are used in the cooler and may be affecting air circulation. GM and attendant were advised to discard leftover portions at the end of breakfast service. GM stated the packets will be placed on another shelf during breakfast tomorrow higher up in the cooler to see if that helps maintain a colder temperature temperature. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

4-602.13 Cabinet beneath the coffee maker in the kitchen was soiled with splash. A little splash was on the wall next to the cabinet as well. 
 --A small counter top fryer was observed in the storage area soiled with grease and food debris on the outside. Used oil and food debris were inside the fryer.
Clean the aforementioned items.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-501.110  (C) Employees were found not using the designated dressing rooms / changing areas or designated employees lockers when changing clothes or storing personal articles. Dressing rooms and lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used if employees regularly change clothes or store personal articles in the establishment while working. Reference 6-501.110. findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Hard cooked eggs and Greek yogurts in the glass front cooler are above 41F. Eggs are 47F and Yogurt in the back is 43F. Yogurt containers in front are 48F. The back of the unit is -01 and the fan is not running. It appears that the unit is freezing up. The foods from top and bottom shelves were discarded. Foods in the middle two shelves were below 41F and transferred to a different holding unit. The glass front unit was unplugged and will be unthawed and watched or serviced to ensure that it functions before foods requiring refrigeration for safety are placed back into the unit. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed

Also, there is no thermometer in the juice holding unit. 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods Provide thermometer for this machine.  shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed that the area in the front o f the juice machine under the nozzles is soiled. Take care to clean this area daily. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Waffel batter and milk gallons do not have date marks. The batter is not kept for more than 3 days by standard operating procedure. However the milk gallons do not hasve a standard time. They are used according to need. Take care to date mark all open TCS, ready to eat foods and use or discard within 7 days. 750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days. Batter and the two open milk gallons were date marked.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Thermometers in the three units in the back are reading zero degrees ferenheight. Three thermometers were available in the drawer in the kitchen and were added to the cold holding units. 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: Salt and pepper along with spray for the waffle iron are observed to be stored on the small area next to the hand sink and under and around the soap dispenser.  Do not used this area to store food. The items were removed. 750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: Employee observed to wash hands and use the paper towel that turned off the handles of the faucet to continue to dry the hands. 750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: Observed the coffee carafes and other food contact items to be drying on towels on the counter top in the kitchen. 750-820a For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing of utensils and equipment, a sink with no fewer then three compartments shall be provided and used in the order of wash rinse sanitize air dry. Provide drying racks for kitchen equipment. Do not dry in contact with absorbent towels.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: No test kit is available for measuring the concentration of the Quat sanitizer used in the kitchen. 750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million. Provide proper test kit.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: Observed the cloth used for wiping to be sitting on the counter. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. Use a wiping cloth bucket to store sanitizer cloth in between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed some crumbs on shelves in dry storage and in cabinets in the kitchen. Clean and maintain free of crumbs and soil. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: Observed single use forks to be sitting in a basket, tines exposed next to the hand wash sink and in close proximity to the soap dispenser.  Also observed the coffee filters to be stored on top of the coffee pot uncovered and unprotected. Store single use items covered and protected from potential contamination. The forks were discarded. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.250 - Boiled eggs in breakfast counter cooler had surface and internal temperatures of 46F-47F and 47F-48F respectively. Eggs were discarded in the trash.

All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41F/below while on display and service.  (see general comments).

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Thermometers were not observed in the breakfast counter cooler or in the fridge/freezer unit used for storage of butter packets and boiled eggs.
A thermometer was placed in the breakfast counter cooler. Another thermometer is needed for the fridge. Provide functioning thermometers for all cold holding units used for storage of potentially hazardous foods. 

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 160 - Breakfast attendant was observed wearing the same pair of gloves for more than one task. Inspector mentioned changing gloves between tasks multiple times during the inspection. Attendant was also advised that hands need to be properly washed periodically/between tasks. Attendant was not observed washing hands at any time before putting on gloves or between tasks. Proper handwashing technique, when to wash hands, and proper glove use were discussed at length (educational handouts also provided).
 
Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food, clean equipment, or unwrapped single service articles.
Gloves shall be single use and used for only one task. Gloves must be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.1210 - The surface of the cabinet next to the wash basin at the 3 part sink is damaged, and the surface is not smooth or easily cleanable. Repair the cabinet to the left of the wash basin so the area is smooth and can be easily maintained clean.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Damp wiping cloth was observed out on the counter. Attendant noted she was using the sanitizer at the 3 part sink with the wiping cloth. Sanitizer solution was prepared in a separate bucket for storage of wiping cloth used for wiping down general surfaces (tables and counters). 

Store wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms. Maintain sanitizer solution at concentration indicated on label (150-400ppm). Change the solution as needed (i.e. solution and/or wiping cloths become heavily soiled), and use test strips to verify solution is at proper concentration. Maintain separate solutions for food contact versus non-food contact surfaces. If spray bottles of sanitizer are used, then disposable paper towels must be used and discarded after each use.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - A) boxes of single service items were observed on the floor in the breakfast storage area. Store containers of single service articles, regardless of packaging, at least 6 inches off the floor.

Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination

B) Some of the plastic knives at the breakfast counter were observed with food contact surfaces presented out of the storage container. Store all utensils within handles presented out so food contact surfaces will not be touched by guests and staff when retrieving utensils. 
(wash hands and wear gloves when stocking utensils from bulk boxes).

Single-service articles shall be stored, handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

Maintain a supply of soap and paper towels at the handsink to allow for proper handwashing.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - A) Floor drain under 3 part sink was soiled with buildup. Clean the floor drain as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

The floor around the drain must be smooth and easily cleanable. The juncture between the floor and cabinets must be sealed to eliminate a potential location for debris to accumulate and/or for pests to hide.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean, including floor drains. The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, including along equipment such as cabinets.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at a proper product temperature of 41F/below at all times during storage. (see general comments).

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.citation_text:
750.540 - Proof of a current Food Manager Certification was not available for any of the full-time staff currently employed at the facility. One member of the staff has her food handler certification but has not yet passed the manager certification. Staff members were certain one of the employees has a current manager certification, but that person was off/out of town at the time of inspection.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed

findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:

750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: CORRECTED> 1) coffee filters to be store on top of coffee machine. 750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.comment:
Observed no light shield inside the Kenmore refrigerator. Provide a light shield for bulb.
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed a soiled mop to be stored in the mop bucket. Hang mops after use to ensure quick drying.
750-1160 The premises shall be kept in such a condition to prevent the harborage or feeding of insects or rodents.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
The coffee dispenser spout and surrounding area are soiled.  Clean and sanitize this area.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Absence of thermometers to the cooling units. Section 750.140 Provode thermometers to all cooling units.
